title: Prioritized edge guardrails for dedicated overflow with model-variant shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a prioritized set of edge guardrails that limit hosted spillover from Dedicated pools while enabling controlled model-variant shedding. Goal: preserve SLOs for P0/P1 tenants on Dedicated capacity during regional pressure without large cost/regression for customers when hosted backfill occurs.
background: We currently have several ad-hoc spillover behaviors when Dedicated capacity is exhausted: immediate hosted routing, naive fair-share throttles, or full request rejection. These lead to either unexpected latency regressions for high-priority tenants or expensive hosted fallbacks at scale. This ticket proposes a deterministic, priority-aware policy that reduces blast radius and gives clear rollback paths.
design_decisions: 1) Priority buckets: tenants are assigned a numeric priority (0-100). Requests inherit tenant priority at request time and are compared against pool headroom. 2) Grace lanes: each Dedicated pool reserves soft lanes (5-15% capacity) for high-priority tenants; these lanes have a longer grace period before eviction. 3) Progressive model-variant shedding: when overflow is needed, prefer demoting to a compatible, lower-cost quantized variant (variant-A -> variant-B -> host-emu) instead of immediate hosted routing. 4) Spillover budget: enforce per-tenant and per-pool token budget for hosted fallbacks; once budget exhausted, circuit-breaker engages. 5) Region affinity with hysteresis: only spill to hosted in same region unless region health < threshold. 6) Observability hooks: emit events for every policy decision with reason codes for tracing and postmortems.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prod-sim): implement decision engine in python service behind a feature flag; simulate policy on historical request traces to tune thresholds. Phase 2 (canary): rollout to 10% of requests for low-risk tenant set with full logging. Phase 3 (gradual): expand to all Dedicated pools with metric-driven ramp. Phase 4: harden with fast-path in C++ runtime and integrate with autoscaler to reclaim lanes dynamically.
rollout_plan: - Toggle-based rollout controlled by config in Console. - Start in us-west-2 Dedicated pools. - Canary with internal tenants and opt-in customers. - 72h watch window, SLO gates (p50/p95 latency, error rate) and cost gates (hosted token spend delta). - Immediate disable path: kill feature flag -> revert to prior routing. - Post-rollout 2-week observation and fine-tuning.
testing_strategy: - Unit tests for decision engine and variant-selection matrix. - Replay historical traffic through prod-sim, measure delta in SLOs and hosted spend. - Fault injection: simulate region outage, sudden traffic spike, and slow model variant to ensure circuit-breakers trigger. - Stress test with synthetic tenants to validate soft lane eviction and grace timers.
metrics: Primary: Dedicated pool SLOs (p50,p95,p99 latency), Dedicated throughput utilization, hosted fallback token spend per tenant, hosted fallback rate, number of variant-shedding events. Secondary: customer error rate, user-perceived latency degradation, KV-cache hit rate for variant transitions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulated historical replay shows <=2% increase in p95 latency for high-priority tenants and <=10% reduction in hosted fallback cost vs naive spillover. 2) Canary period passes SLO gates for 72h without error bursts. 3) Circuit-breaker correctly engages when per-tenant hosted budget exhausted. 4) Observability produces traceable reason codes for every spillover decision.
open_questions: - How should we encode tenant priority in our IAM/DB so that it is immutable for request evaluation? - Do we allow customers to opt out of model-variant shedding? (privacy/regulatory concerns) - Cache consistency: when a request demotes to a different variant, can we reuse KV cache across variants safely? Need further perf tests. - Billing model: how do we report mixed-variant token billing to customers?
notes: Decisions from initial architecture review (2026-03-05): prefer soft lanes over strict reservations to improve utilization. Variant-shedding must be reversible at request granularity to avoid long-term correctness issues. Diego will prototype decision engine; Maya will own observability contract.
